A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CDCL-NLI dataset and RST-based inference framework. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. v1 ends after its references; v2 includes readable Appendices A–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation assessments, model comparisons, ablations and cross-lingual experiments, including Tables 2 and 4–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations and analyses in the main text and appendices, including Tables 3–5 and 8–9, threshold sensitivity and case studies.

M1.justification: The encoder, RST graph fusion, 0.8 lexical threshold, two-layer attention network and EDU attribution remain. The objective changes from 0.4 Lexp + Lcls + 0.3 Ltriplet to 0.2 Lexp + 0.8(Lcls + Ltriplet), a limited revision to loss weighting (v1 Equation 15; v2 Equation 7).

E1.justification: v2 adds an English-translated CDCL-NLI test scenario and reports translation-based expansion of premise documents. The news domain, 370 events, 26 languages and DocNLI benchmark remain. The large increase in instance counts primarily changes experimental scale rather than establishing new topic or language coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds hypothesis-only and Qwen3-8B comparisons in Table 3. It also introduces R2F into the cross-lingual transfer comparison and adds Qwen3, DocNLI and R2F to single-document comparisons previously reported only for the proposed method.

E3.justification: Dataset splits change from 666/222/222 to 22,200/1,605/1,605, with v2 explicitly specifying event-disjoint partitioning. The proposed model's learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 1e-5, batch size from 32 to 16, and epochs from 10 to 20. Llama LoRA settings change, the main LLM comparison uses few-shot prompting, and explanation evaluation adds ROUGE and METEOR.

E4.justification: v2 adds a hypothesis-artifact diagnostic, a displayed lexical-threshold sensitivity analysis, language-pair/EDU distribution analyses, and detailed model and LLM case studies. Existing component and single-document ablations are retained and extended through English-language controls and additional comparators.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance. Annotation agreement values and their reporting practice are unchanged between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 6; the new distribution plots describe dataset characteristics.

E6.justification: Main CDCL-NLI results are replaced under revised data and settings: v1 reports 72.03 test macro F1, while v2 reports 68.95 cross-lingual and 70.68 English macro F1. These are not same-setting performance changes. v2 adds baseline, prompting and explanation-metric results. The DocNLI comparison remains numerically identical, and v2's transfer table retains all 20 earlier test scores while replacing development scores with R2F results.

T1.justification: The formal total-objective definition changes so that lambda weights classification and triplet losses jointly rather than triplet loss alone. The RST definitions, attention equations and individual triplet-loss expression otherwise remain equivalent, with detailed formulas relocated to Appendix B. No theoretical guarantees or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The new-task, RST-fusion, interpretability and broad superiority claims remain. v2 updates the dataset contribution from 1,110 to 25,410 instances, introduces a claimed 'at least 3.5%' advantage, and shifts suggested applications from semantic retrieval toward hallucination elimination. These revise the existing contribution narrative without redefining its central novelty.

C2.justification: v2 interprets hypothesis-only performance as evidence of limited artifacts, English controls as exposing language barriers, and Qwen's thinking mode as explaining its strength. It explicitly states the document-pair limitation and removes v1's language-family transfer explanations and several future directions. Appendix E additionally asserts computational advantages without reporting timing measurements.

D1.justification: Appendices A–D add annotation criteria, complete generation/training/evaluation prompts, relation inventories, baseline hyperparameters and input-length limits. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's brief settings description. Conversely, v1's numerical triplet margins and weight decay are no longer specified. The linked resource address is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes retrieval-focused motivation and references, drops discussion of InferSent and LIME, and adds Qwen3, chain-of-thought and LLM interpretability work, including Wei et al. and Singh et al. The sentence/document-level taxonomy and claimed gap in joint cross-document, cross-lingual NLI remain.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method exposition and experimental discussion are extensively condensed and rewritten. Task formulation moves into the dataset section, technical material moves into appendices, and conclusions, limitations and ethics become separate sections. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 redraws introductory and method diagrams, merges main comparisons and ablations into a dual-test table, redesigns single-document plots, and replaces the explanation bar chart with a radar chart. It adds distribution plots, a threshold plot, prompt panels and EDU case tables. The annotation table and language pie chart are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through explicit event-disjoint splits, hypothesis-only and English-language controls, and detailed prompts and baseline settings. These address gaps in v1's experimental documentation. Benefits are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: the claimed 1.89-point cross-lingual ablation drop is 3.09 points in Table 3, and Figure 10 leaves its task-performance scale unspecified. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
